newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-FIFA STILL KEEN ON WORLD CUP WITHOUT FENCES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA STILL KEEN ON WORLD CUP WITHOUT FENCES.

text.p: International soccer chiefs are expected to tell organisers of next year's World Cup finals in France on Friday that they would rather not have spectators fenced in at the tournament.

France plans to keep fences at most of its grounds during the finals and the sports world governing body FIFA said on Thursday it recognised the French government was responsible for security but still hoped that a flexible solution could be found.
FIFA's World Cup organising committee is due to meet here on Friday when the subject is almost certainly to be discussed.

"The FIFA committee for security and fair play has reiterated its opinion that football matches should be played in stadiums without fences but has acknowledged that, as the French government has accepted full responsibility for security ... the fences may have to remain," FIFA said in a statement.
The governing body plans to look closely at an international tournament in France next month when matches will be played in some of the World Cup stadiums.
"We hope a flexible solution may yet be found in this matter," FIFA said.
Soccer officials are worried that fans tend to behave badly when they are "caged in" and want to avoid a repeat of past disasters when spectators have died after being crushed against fences.
The success of last year's largely trouble-free European championship in England, where there were no fences, has also boosted the argument in favour of taking down the cages.
